gen-almendra-display-gf-noto-sans-osage: Almendra Display carries an ornate, bookish flourish, with letters that never pinch shut. Noto Sans Osage meets it with round, inflated lowercase bowls, and that generous fullness is the pair's best quality.
gen-fs-bonny-fs-epilogue: Literary and refined, Bonny sets tight lines with gently gaping curves. Epilogue brings a wiry, monoline body with tall lowercase and stubby ascenders, and a modest bump in its size would let it hold its own.
gen-almendra-display-gf-noto-sans-pahawh: Almendra Display has a pronounced x-height and letters that refuse to pinch shut, which gives it an ornate, storybook look. Noto Sans Pahawh Hmong follows with a high-set x-height and rounds like a cracked bangle, so paragraphs would feel contemporary and open.
gen-audiowide-gf-noto-sans-kayah-li: Chrome-bright and futuristic, Audiowide draws tile-like glyphs with no thick-thin shift. Noto Sans Kayah Li is the quieter worker, lifting its brush ends before curves close, while Audiowide handles the spectacle.
gen-eater-gf-noto-sans-osmanya: Noto Sans Osmanya has wide, easy s shapes and a lowercase that looks oversized beside its capitals. And Eater's dark, aggressive heading, with its short ascenders, gives way to text that would read smoothly, clean and unhurried, paragraph after paragraph.
gen-almendra-display-gf-noto-sans-pau-ci: Noto Sans Pau Cin Hau has open-ended curves and only a short step from lowercase to capital height. But Almendra Display, ornate and literary, gives the pair its strongest quality: a sense of old-world flourish resting on a modern base.
gen-eater-gf-stack-sans-notch: Eater's thin strokes sit beside moderately weighty stems, with wide gaps between letters, which gives it a dark, aggressive bite. And Stack Sans Notch answers with open curves and rod-stock lines of identical thickness, so the heading's drama sits above a steady, big-bodied text.
gen-audiowide-gf-noto-sans-mayan-numeral: Wide-grouted, tile-like and futuristic, Audiowide never flickers between thick and thin strokes. Noto Sans Mayan Numerals does the quieter job, with tall-bodied small letters and a visibly gaping c, while Audiowide handles the show.
gen-fs-bonny-fs-supreme: Tight-set and literary, Bonny has gaping curves and a mid-range gap between its boldest and faintest strokes. And Supreme adds a heavy-looking, crisp strip of sans-serif text through the middle, with letters held open rather than curled shut.
gen-eater-gf-stack-sans-text: Aggressive and dark, Eater steps softly from heavy to light strokes, with short ascenders and wide gaps between letters. Stack Sans Text reads like pencil that never presses harder.
